item.title: Beyond Predictable Paths: Redefining AI Security Incident Reporting for Agents
item.description:
The paper outlines what data should be captured when an AI agent is attacked, highlighting that current incident-reporting standards miss key AI‑specific details. The authors surveyed 23 experts and produced a checklist of information needed for compliant AI‑agent incident reports. The result is a proposed framework that could help organisations meet legal and governance requirements when securing AI agents.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure that hosts AI agents, here is what to do: 1) Update your incident‑reporting templates to include the AI‑agent‑specific fields identified in the paper (e.g., model version, data sources, and agent behaviour logs). 2) Train your security teams to capture and log these fields during any incident. 3) Verify compliance with the new framework before reporting to regulators or clients.

item.title: Structured Decomposition for Reliable LLM-Generated Access Control Policies
item.description:
This research introduces a tool that turns natural‑language access control rules into Rego code for OPA, with automatic validation and test generation to ensure reliability. It builds a full pipeline that detects policies, extracts components, checks against schemas, lints, compiles, and runs tests. The result is higher confidence that the policies you deploy are correct and secure.

IT Breakdown: If you manage OPA in your cloud, 1) feed your NLACPs to the tool to auto‑generate Rego, 2) run the built‑in tests to confirm correctness, 3) merge the output into your CI/CD pipeline for continuous validation.

item.title: When the Agent Becomes the Kernel: A Systematization of Security on the Path to AI-Native Operating Systems
item.description:
Large‑language‑model agents now act like operating‑system kernels, making changes to code, mail, and purchases without a trusted mediator. The authors propose a security framework that ensures any agent action is mediated by a provenance check, giving a deterministic way to verify trust. The result is a set of design principles that could guide the creation of AI‑native OSes and similar systems.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure, check whether your automated agents (e.g., CI/CD pipelines, auto‑scaling scripts, AI‑assistants) perform all privileged actions through a provenance‑based mediator; if not, add a layer that records and validates each agent’s action history before execution. This flags a risk: if your organisation uses any AI‑powered automation without such checks, immediately audit for unmediated access paths.

item.title: One to More, More to One: Category-Aware Iterative Expert Training for Software Engineering Agents
item.description:
The study tackles uneven performance across different software engineering task categories when using reinforcement learning agents. It introduces a category‑aware training framework, including a task construction tool and an evidence‑based labeling system, which together raise overall training success rates. This is directly relevant for IT teams that deploy AI agents in multi‑domain development workflows.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud‑based AI agents for software engineering, step 1: identify the task categories your agents handle and note any performance dips. Step 2: integrate a category‑aware training pipeline that isolates and trains on each category separately, using a label system to validate results. Step 3: merge the specialised policies back into your main agent and monitor for improved, balanced performance across all categories.

item.title: [News] GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models
item.description: Microsoft Research has introduced GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash, two efficient pathology foundation models that reduce computational demands while preserving performance. These models enable larger population-scale studies in pathology by lowering the resource barrier for research.

item.title: [News] Transformers now runs llama.cpp quants
item.description: Hugging Face has added support for running llama.cpp quantized models directly within the Transformers library, enabling efficient local inference for large language models. This allows developers to deploy powerful LLMs on resource-constrained hardware without cloud reliance.

item.title: [News] Better prompt caching for GPT-6
item.description: OpenAI has released GPT-6, featuring enhanced prompt caching that boosts cache hit rates, adds diagnostics, explicit breakpoints, and controls to lower latency and cost. These improvements aim to make large language model interactions more efficient and predictable for developers.

item.title: [News] Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna
item.description: OpenAI has unveiled two new models, GPT‑6 Sol and GPT‑6 Luna, offering different balances of capability and cost for everyday work. These models extend the frontier of AI performance and may influence how businesses integrate advanced language models into their operations.

item.title: [News] Qualcomm launches two new smartphone chips with emphasis on AI
item.description: Qualcomm has announced two new smartphone chips that support running 30‑billion‑parameter mixture‑of‑expert models directly on device. This pushes local AI inference closer to the edge, potentially reducing latency and data‑center dependency for mobile workloads.
